etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin relātus, perfect passive participle of referō (“carry back; report”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To tell in a descriptive way.
(transitive) To bring into a relation, association, or connection (between one thing and another).

quote.citation: 2002, Paul Light, Karen Littleton, Learning with Computers: Analysing Productive Interactions, page 92:
quote.text: The use of video made it possible to relate the talk to the answers given to particular problems in the test. With this research design it was possible to relate changes in test score measures to changes in linguistic features […]

definitions.definition: (intransitive, with to) To identify with; to understand.

quote.citation: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book III, Canto IX”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC, stanza 51:
quote.text: Abate your zealous haste, till morrow next again / Both light of heaven and strength of men relate.
